categories.main_business_segments: Kyorin Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. operates primarily in the pharmaceutical business, focusing on the research, development, manufacturing, and sales of prescription drugs. The group consists of the parent company, two consolidated subsidiaries (Kyorin Remedio and Kyorin Pharmaceutical Group Factory), and one equity-method affiliate (Nihon Rikagaku Yakuhin). The company is structured as a single business segment centered on pharmaceuticals, including both new drugs and generic drugs.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include small molecule drug discovery, innovative drug development based on novel mechanisms of action, and the integration of external technologies and modalities. Manufacturing is conducted under strict GMP compliance, with a focus on high-quality and stable supply. The company also utilizes advanced production facilities and invests in research infrastructure, such as the Watarase Drug Discovery Center.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kyorin’s primary customers are medical institutions and healthcare professionals in Japan, with a focus on hospitals and clinics. The company’s main end markets are the Japanese prescription pharmaceutical market, with some overseas sales through licensing and alliances. Major wholesalers such as Alfresa, Medipal, Suzuken, and Toho Yakuhin account for significant portions of sales.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are predominantly domestic, with over 90% of sales and assets located in Japan. While it has some international activities through licensing and alliances (notably with partners in the US, Europe, and Asia), its manufacturing, R&D, and sales infrastructure are concentrated in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kyorin operates mainly in the midstream and downstream segments of the pharmaceutical supply chain, encompassing drug discovery, development, manufacturing, and direct sales to wholesalers and medical institutions. It also engages in upstream activities through in-house R&D and external in-licensing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Kyorin is focused on strengthening its new drug pipeline, maximizing the ratio of new drugs in its portfolio, and expanding through both in-house innovation and external licensing. R&D is concentrated on areas such as pulmonary fibrosis, pain, and autoimmune diseases, with an emphasis on novel mechanisms and new modalities. The company is also pursuing digital health solutions and aims to enhance sustainability and corporate governance.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of prescription pharmaceuticals to wholesalers, supplemented by royalty income, milestone payments from licensing agreements, and contract manufacturing. The company also receives one-time payments from out-licensing its proprietary compounds to global partners.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kyorin competes with major Japanese and global pharmaceutical companies in the prescription drug market, particularly in respiratory, urology, and infectious disease segments. It is a mid-sized player with a strong domestic presence and a reputation for high-quality, innovative products, but faces competition from both large multinationals and generic manufacturers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥130.1 billion (approx. $830 million), with operating profit of ¥12.6 billion and net profit of ¥9.1 billion. The company has shown steady growth, with an 8.8% year-on-year increase in sales and a significant rise in profitability, driven by new drug sales and licensing income. The group employs approximately 2,000 people.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kyorin emphasizes its ability to deliver high-value, innovative new drugs that address unmet medical needs, particularly in specialty therapeutic areas. The company differentiates itself through a robust R&D pipeline, high product quality, reliable supply, and strong relationships with healthcare professionals. Its focus on both proprietary and in-licensed products, as well as digital health initiatives, enhances its competitive edge.
